title: Two tiers on two hosts run at the same time
name: Two tiers on two hosts run at the same
description:
The point of the feature: low on OpenCode, mid on Codex, high on Claude Code, all burning under one `dispatch.concurrency`. Nothing in core should assume one host per board any more.

One integration test proves it: two ready nodes scored to two tiers, `dispatch.tiers` pointing at two of the fake hosts in test/integration/hosts, `sober run a b`. Both start, both run records name their own host, each log renders through its own adapter (`renderLine` in hosts.ts already picks by event shape), and `--watch` on the Codex-tier node is refused by tier while the Claude-tier node is attended. The same pair started by the unattended queue (packages/core/src/queue.ts, ADR 0056) resolves the host per node, not once for the batch.

Fix whatever the test finds that assumes a single host — the batch probe, the per-run host string, anything keyed by `config.dispatch.host`. No new surface; this node is the test and the fixes it forces.

brief.approach: Add a real-git integration case in test/integration/dispatch.test.ts using two existing fake host adapters from test/integration/hosts. Configure dispatch.concurrency=2, score two approved nodes into distinct dispatch.tiers, and call the CLI run wave. Assert overlap in their run intervals, each run record's host and tier, and each host-specific rendered log. Exercise attended refusal for the Codex-tier host and attended acceptance for the Claude-tier host. Add the same pair to test/integration/queue.test.ts with queue approvals and verify each queued run resolves its own host. Trace any failure to packages/core/src/dispatch.ts dispatchWave/resolveHost or packages/core/src/queue.ts runQueue and fix only the shared assumption; avoid new configuration or UI. Use narrow tests during development; commit only after the checks pass.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run --project integration test/integration/dispatch.test.ts test/integration/queue.test.ts
acceptance.proves: Two simultaneous ready nodes and the queued pair use their own tier hosts, preserve host-specific records and logs, and enforce attended capability per node.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec biome check test/integration/dispatch.test.ts test/integration/queue.test.ts packages/core/src/dispatch.ts packages/core/src/queue.ts && pnpm --filter @besober/core build
acceptance.proves: Touched integration and core code passes style checks and core builds.

plain.what: Prove that one board can run nodes on two different hosts at the same time, and fix any shared-host assumption the test exposes.
plain.why: The queue and run wave already select hosts per node, but no combined test protects that behavior.
plain.check: Run only the dispatch and queue integration tests, then style and core build checks.
plain.risk: The test may expose a shared-host assumption in dispatch or queue; changes stay within those paths.
